perturbation.note: The pool choice moves a model's win rate by this much. A swap between two adjacent models needs the DIFFERENCE of their shifts to exceed the gap between them, hence sd*sqrt(2).

gaussian_route.note: The Gaussian swap route assumes the two models' shifts are independent draws from the CROSS-MODEL dispersion, giving sd*sqrt(2). The bootstrap measures the sampling sd of each adjacent pair's shift DIFFERENCE directly, and it is about half that. Substituting the measured value brings the independent-union estimate back to the bootstrap's displacement rate; the assumed value roughly doubles it.

calibration_of_the_illustrative_model.note: The K=6 row of by_leaderboard_size agrees with the bootstrap only under UNIFORM spacing. Run the identical simulation on the observed gaps and it disagrees badly, because sd_of_shift is the dispersion of six models' realised shifts, not the sampling sd of one model's shift (measured at sd_shift_difference_measured, roughly half the sqrt(2)x value the Gaussian route assumes). The agreement at K=6 uniform is therefore a coincidence of two compensating errors and must not be reported as a validation of the model.

unanimous_subset.note: Same item bootstrap on the 2,885 comparisons where BOTH pools are internally unanimous - the population the headline divergence rates describe - so the displacement rate can be quoted for that population rather than only for the full corpus under the default tie-break.

bootstrap.resampling_unit: prompt cluster (98.2% of rows sit in a doubled prompt)
bootstrap.note: Resamples items and recomputes BOTH leaderboards. The rate at which displacement occurs here is the honest read on how decisive the observed zero-displacement result is.

threshold.note: by_leaderboard_size is an ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO, not a measurement. It holds the measured per-model shift SD fixed, assumes those shifts are iid Gaussian across models, and spreads K models uniformly across the observed win-rate span. p_any_displacement is Monte Carlo over per-model shifts, so adjacent pairs correctly share a model; the indep_product column is the naive closed form kept for comparison. None of these is a lower bound: real arenas cluster more tightly than uniform (raising displacement) but correlated shifts across models lower it, and we have not measured that correlation.
